 KUCHING : Kuching City FC head coach Aidil Sharin Sahak has challenged his side to rise to the occasion against Gangwon FC as the Cats chase their first victory in the AFC Champions League Two (ACL2) at Gangneung Stadium, South Korea tomorrow (Oct 29).
 With both sides sitting on one point after two Group H matches, the meeting presents an opportunity for either team to reignite its campaign.
 Aidil expects a fiercely contested encounter, with Kuching City FC needing to stay disciplined, adapt to the conditions and make their chances count.
 “Both teams need to win and both teams are at the same point now.
 “So definitely, you’re going to see two teams that are going to fight for a win,” he said during the pre-match press conference today (Oct 28).
 The Cats head into the contest after drawing 1-1 with Hong Kong’s Kitchee SC, while Gangwon suffered a 2-1 defeat to Phnom Penh Crown in their previous ACL2 outing.
 Aidil acknowledged that the South Korean side had endured disappointing results but warned that tomorrow’s clash would bring an entirely different challenge.
 With colder weather adding another hurdle, the squad have been working to adjust ahead of kick-off.
 Aidil said the team would concentrate on its own game plan and use its final training session to prepare for the conditions.
 “The weather is not good and it is getting cold, but the boys are adapting well.
 “Today is our last day of training, and hopefully tomorrow we can put up a good fight against our opponents,” he added.
 Kuching City FC’s midfielder Petrus Shitembi echoed his coach’s assessment, describing Gangwon as a young, energetic side likely to draw strength from playing in front of its home supporters.
 However, he believes Kuching City have plenty to play for and will not travel to South Korea simply to make up the numbers.
 “We expect a very tough match, but we have a lot to play for as well.
 “We are looking forward to trying to cause an upset because we need to put ourselves in a position where we still have a chance in the competition,” he said.
